Compatibility with Cucumber

Source: vignettes/compatibility.qmd

cucumber doesn’t just follow the Cucumber documentation. Its tests run the official projects’ own test data, copied from their repositories, and expect the same results:

Official project What cucumber checks against it
Compatibility Kit Each of its 47 runnable samples runs with CucumberMessagesReporter, and the messages must be the ones the official implementations give: the same messages, in the same order, with the same ids, statuses, pickles, attachments and results. The JUnit XML of each sample is compared too
Gherkin Every good and bad file of its test data must give the official source, document, pickles and errors
Cucumber Expressions Its test data for matching, parsing and tokenizing must give the official results and errors
Tag expressions Its evaluation test data
Messages Every message cucumber writes must follow the official JSON schema
HTML formatter CucumberHtmlReporter embeds the official report

The differences are few, and each is deliberate:

  • Fields that depend on the machine or the language are not compared: where files are, timestamps, durations, error messages and stack traces, and the text of snippets, which are R code.
  • R signals pending() and skip_scenario() as conditions, so those results have an exception, unlike the samples where the step returns the status.
  • {bigdecimal} and {biginteger} aren’t built in, as R has no numbers of any precision.
  • Cucumber’s Markdown parser gives a header-less first line a Feature without a keyword, which its own schema rejects. cucumber does the same and exempts that one document from the schema.

Step definitions are R functions, so what the official projects say about types of a specific language, like Java’s, doesn’t apply.
